blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (for example `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). Every lookup that matches no customer reaches `errorHandler` in `src/server.ts`, which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, so the typed e-mail address of a person — customer or not — lands in the application logs with no stated purpose or retention (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e)). The same applies, to a lesser extent, to the customer id in `no customer ${id}` at src/support.ts:32.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: The proposal's stated purpose is that the Helply widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to"; that needs the opaque id and the name, not the phone number, birth date, address or e-mail address. Every signed-in customer who opens the chat sends all of them to Helply, a third-party processor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 25, Art. 28). Send only `id` and `name`, and select only those columns in `customerById` for this route.
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change adds Helply as a recipient of customer data, but neither the proposal nor the code says whether a processing agreement (Art. 28) is in place, where Helply stores the data (Chapter V transfers outside the EEA), how long it keeps it, or whether customer erasure reaches the copy held by Helply (Art. 17). State these in the proposal; only the controller can answer them.
findings.title: Helply processor and transfer not identified

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The lookup exists so agents need not ask customers who they are; the route returns the whole record, birth date and postal address included, to every user with the `support` role. Whether agents need those fields depends on support procedures not visible here (for example identity checks); if they do not, select and return only the fields the purpose needs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: Support lookup returns more than identifying the customer needs
